arxiv-2110-04299.title: Superdiffusion in self-reinforcing run-and-tumble model with rests
arxiv-2110-04299.creator: Sergei Fedotov, Daniel Han, Alexey O. Ivanov, Marco A. A. da Silva
arxiv-2110-04299.description: Abstract This paper introduces a run-and-tumble model with self-reinforcing directionality and rests. We derive a single governing hyperbolic partial differential equation for the probability density of random walk position, from which we obtain the second moment in the long time limit. We find the criteria for the transition between superdiffusion and diffusion caused by the addition of a rest state.

arxiv-2208-02411.title: Impact of the Consistency Model on Checkpointing of Distributed Shared Memory Thanks: This work is funded in part by award 1849599 and award CNS1816487 from the National Science Foundation. The views and conclusions contained in this document are those of the authors and should not be interpreted as
arxiv-2208-02411.creator: Sandeep Kulkarni, Duong Nguyen, Lewis Tseng, Nitin Vaidya
arxiv-2208-02411.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Sandeep Kulkarni, Duong Nguyen, Lewis Tseng, Nitin Vaidya. In this report, we consider the impact of the consistency model on checkpointing and rollback algorithms for distributed shared memory. In particular, we consider specific implementations of four consistency models for distributed shared memory, namely, linearizability, sequential consistency, causal consistency and eventual consistency, and develop checkpointing and rollback algorithms that can be integrated into the implementations of the consistency models.

arxiv-2208-05065.title: Fixed-time Integral Sliding Mode Control for Admittance Control of a Robot Manipulator Publication type: Article Type
arxiv-2208-05065.creator: Yuzhu Sun, Mien Van*, Stephen McIlvanna, Seán McLoone, Dariusz Ceglarek, Sun Y, Van M, McIlvanna S, McLoone S, Ceglarek D
arxiv-2208-05065.description: Abstract This paper proposes a novel fixed-time integral sliding mode controller for admittance control to enhance physical human-robot collaboration. The proposed method combines the benefits of compliance to external forces of admittance control and high robustness to uncertainties of integral sliding mode control (ISMC), such that the system can collaborate with a human partner in an uncertain environment effectively.

arxiv-2212-13179.title: Mining Architectural Information: A Systematic Mapping Study
arxiv-2212-13179.creator: Musengamana Jean de Dieu, Peng Liang, Mojtaba Shahin, Chen Yang, Zengyang Li
arxiv-2212-13179.description: Abstract Mining Software Repositories (MSR) has become an essential activity in software development. Mining architectural information (e.g., architectural models) to support architecting activities, such as architecture understanding, has received significant attention in recent years. However, there is a lack of clarity on what literature on mining architectural information is available.

arxiv-2306-10226.title: Skyrmions at Finite Density
arxiv-2306-10226.creator: Fabrizio Canfora, Scarlett C. Rebolledo-Caceres
arxiv-2306-10226.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Fabrizio Canfora, Scarlett C. Rebolledo-Caceres. In this paper, we will describe recent advances in analytical methods to construct exact solutions of the Skyrme model (and its generalizations) representing inhomogeneous Hadronic condensates living at finite Baryon density. Such novel analytical tools are based on the idea to generalize the well known spherical hedgehog ansatz to situations (relevant for the analysis of finite density effects) in which there is no spherical symmetry anymore.

arxiv-2312-12739.title: What is the correct definition of entropy for general relativistic field theory?
arxiv-2312-12739.description: Abstract Recently, the author and collaborators proposed a method to construct a new conserved charge different from the Noether one for general relativistic field theory on curved space-time with energy-momentum tensor covariantly conserved, and that the new conserved charge describes the entropy of the system.

arxiv-2506-09828.title: CONTINUITY OF THE SUPERPOTENTIALS AND SLICES OF TROPICAL CURRENTS
arxiv-2506-09828.creator: Farhad Babaee, Tien Cuong Dinh
arxiv-2506-09828.description: Abstract . We study the question of the continuity of slices of currents and explain how it relates to several seemingly unrelated problems in tropical geometry. On the one hand, through this lens, we show that the continuity of superpotentials constitutes a very general instance of stable intersection theory in tropical geometry.

arxiv-2602-20088.title: Chemotaxis of cell aggregates: morphology and dynamics of migrating active droplets
arxiv-2602-20088.creator: Giulia L. Celora 1, Benjamin J. Walker 3, Mohit P. Dalwadi 2,3, Philip Pearce 3,4
arxiv-2602-20088.description: Abstract Biological tissues have been observed to display emergent fluid-like properties, owing to physical interactions between cells. However, it remains unclear in general how these fluid-like properties affect tissue structure and function. Here, we are motivated by recent experiments in which cell aggregates were observed to behave as active droplets during collective migration along chemical gradients, or chemotaxis.

pmc-10508290.title: Case report: Misdiagnosis of primary mucinous cystadenoma of the testicle by ultrasound
pmc-10508290.creator: Linlin Zhang, Jianyuan Xuan, Manxi Li, Mei Zhang, Yu Song, Ziang Pan, Bo Fan, Lin Lu, Hongyan Zhou, Yang Li
pmc-10508290.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Testicular mucinous cystadenoma is a rare benign testicular tumor with the characteristics of being potentially malignant and showing atypical clinical symptoms; this article reports a case of a primary testicular mucinous cystadenoma misdiagnosed as testicular teratoma by ultrasound. A 69-year-old man was admitted to the hospital because of a 1-year history of left-sided testicular enlargement with scrotal swelling and no obvious abnormalities on laboratory tests.

pmc-10531632.title: Perceived Injustice in Cancer Survivors: Population-Specific Cut-Off Score and Relations with Personal Factors, Symptoms and Quality of Life—A Cross-Sectional Study
pmc-10531632.creator: Eva Roose, Eva Huysmans, Astrid Lahousse, Kenza Mostaqim, Lotte van Gerven, Moniek Vissers, Jo Nijs, Paul Van Wilgen, David Beckwée, Annick Timmermans, Rinske Bults, Laurence Leysen, Eng Ooi
pmc-10531632.description: Fatigue and pain are the most common side effects impacting quality of life (QoL) in cancer survivors. Recent insights have shown that perceived injustice (PI) can play a substantial role in these side effects, but research on cancer survivors is scarce. Furthermore, guidelines for recognizing clinically relevant levels of PI in cancer survivors are missing.

pmc-13138463.title: Comparable Outcomes and Implant Survivorship of Total Knee Arthroplasty After High Tibial Osteotomy and Primary Arthroplasty
pmc-13138463.creator: Eva A. Bax, Rana A. Ahmad, Sean C. Clark, Roel J.H. Custers, Michael J. Taunton, Rafael J. Sierra, Daniel B.F. Saris, Mario Hevesi
pmc-13138463.description: Background:Total knee arthroplasty (TKA) is the treatment of choice for end-stage knee osteoarthritis in many patients. In younger patients with predominantly medial compartment disease, high tibial osteotomy (HTO) is performed as a joint-preserving treatment. However, concerns remain regarding potentially compromised outcomes of TKA after previous HTO given the axial deviation, osteotomy site, secondary surgery, previous hardware, and instrumentation.

pmc-13397848.title: Association of Sleep Patterns and Sleep Quality with Academic Performance Among Female University Students: Insights Supporting SDG 3 (Good Health and Well-Being)
pmc-13397848.creator: Noorah Saleh Al-Sowayan, Lama Essam Aboselmiya
pmc-13397848.description: Background: Sleep quality plays an essential role in cognitive performance, memory consolidation, learning efficiency, and overall wellbeing. University students are particularly vulnerable to sleep disturbances because of academic stress, irregular sleep schedules, and lifestyle-related factors. Poor sleep quality has been associated with impaired academic performance and reduced cognitive functioning.
